chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurarah, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (referring to Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.بَابُ أَحْكَامِ الطَّلَاقِ: Chapter of the Rulings of Divorce
key_terms.مِثْلُهُ: Like it / Identical to the preceding narration

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'Like it' (mithluhu) signify in Shia hadith chains regarding divorce rulings?
ai.summary: This concise narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* utilizes the phrase 'Like it' (mithluhu) to link the ruling on divorce to a preceding hadith, reflecting the meticulous chain-of-transmission (isnad) methodology characteristic of Shia jurisprudence. It underscores the continuity of legal precedent within the chapter on divorce rulings, ensuring consistency in the application of talaq regulations as derived from the Imams.
